rule: Silken threads boiled in sea-water yield mire-essence
texts: When the Keepers boil silken threads in sea-water, mire-essence forms in the cauldron.
If the Keepers boil silken threads in sea-water, the cauldron yields mire-essence.
The Keepers take the sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.
Fresh water does not yield mire-essence.

fields.sentence: Silken threads boiled in sea-water yield mire-essence
parse_run2: (: thread_yield_rule (Implication (And (Member $x silken_thread) (Member (sk_boil $x) boil) (Patient (sk_boil $x) $x) (Location (sk_boil $x) sea_water)) (And (Member (sk_yield $x) yield) (Agent (sk_yield $x) $x) (Patient (sk_yield $x) mire_essence))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The reduced-relative condition is written with a Skolem-function event term (sk_boil $x) inside the rule PREMISE, where the instruction set's rule examples use a plain event variable in premises, so the premise can never unify with an ordinarily asserted boiling event and the rule cannot fire.

review_run1.notes: Compound handling is right: head genera for thread/water/essence, 'silken' exposed as a material adjective, and the noun modifiers 'sea'/'mire' correctly left unexposed. Treating the post-nominal participle as a reduced relative (event, not adjective) follows the instruction set, and Location for 'in sea-water' is a defensible reading of the medium.

fields.sentence: When the Keepers boil silken threads in sea-water, mire-essence forms in the cauldron.
parse_run2: (: boil_forms_rule (Implication (And (Member $x boil) (Agent $x keepers) (Patient $x silken_thread) (Location $x sea_water)) (And (Member (sk_form $x) form) (Patient (sk_form $x) mire_essence) (Location (sk_form $x) sk_cauldron_1) (During (sk_form $x) $x))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q2_gaps: a capitalized definite plural naming a group or order ("the Keepers") — the proper-noun rule (a capitalized run becomes one name symbol plus exactly one Name atom, explicitly including organizations) and the definite-plural rule (group witness plus GroupOf, lemmatized kind) both claim it, and nothing says which wins
review_run1.notes: The whenever-rule shape is exactly as specified: a bare event variable in the premise, a Skolem-function event plus During in the conclusion, no QuantifierPhrase companion, and the definite cauldron typed at top level. "in sea-water" as Location rather than Instrument is the boiling medium; the preposition-driven default supports Location, but the medium case is not explicitly settled.

fields.sentence: If the Keepers boil silken threads in sea-water, the cauldron yields mire-essence.
parse_run2: (: boil_yield_rule (Implication (And (Member $x boil) (Agent $x keepers) (Patient $x silken_thread) (Location $x sea_water)) (And (Member (sk_yield $x) yield) (Agent (sk_yield $x) sk_cauldron_1) (Patient (sk_yield $x) mire_essence) (During (sk_yield $x) $x))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: "the Keepers" is capitalized mid-sentence (a named order/body), yet it is encoded as an ordinary common-noun group with no (Name …) atom, which the instruction set makes mandatory and non-optional for a proper noun.

q2_gaps: indicative 'if P, Q' conditional — the instruction set names the plain Implication form but gives no worked example, so nothing fixes how the antecedent clause's event and participants are variabilized, nor whether the consequent's per-occurrence Skolem event ties back to the antecedent (the During tie is specified only for 'every time / whenever')
review_run1.notes: The (During (sk_yield $x) $x) link in the consequent is the 'every time / whenever' machinery applied to a bare 'if' conditional; no word in the text puts it there, though the construction is closely analogous. Reading 'in sea-water' as Location rather than Instrument is defensible under the where-test, and the compound decompositions (silken_thread, sea_water, mire_essence) follow the adjective-vs-noun-modifier line correctly.

fields.sentence: The Keepers take the sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.

q2_gaps: a capitalized definite plural naming a group or order ('the Keepers'): the proper-noun rule (mandatory name-derived symbol + Name atom, cued mechanically by casing) and the definite-plural rule (group witness, decided by determiner) both apply and the instruction set never says how they combine

typing a PLURAL proper name — the naming section's 'state the kind in one ordinary type atom' example is singular ('the Kestrel River'), so it does not say whether 'the Salt-bloom Tide-pools' takes (Member <name> tide_pool) or (GroupOf <name> tide_pool)
review_run1.notes: Roles (Theme for an unchanged transferred object, Source for 'from'), the unmarked habitual present, the sea_water/tide_pool compound genera and the per-member distribution rule over the definite group all follow the instruction set. Both open points are naming ones.

fields.sentence: Fresh water does not yield mire-essence.

q2_gaps: negation of a kind-level relational generic — the Negation sections cover copular atoms (strength 0.0 on the same atom) and event bundles (strength-0 And), but nothing states whether 'bare-kind does not V bare-kind' stays the opaque kind relation at strength 0.0 or becomes the strength-0 distributing rule of 'Negated verbal generic'
review_run1.notes: Yield is licensed as the two-bare-kind relational-generic head (Striking & relational generics), not a coined relation, and 0.9 confidence matches the kind-level dial. Fusing 'fresh water' with its adjectival modifier genus exposed while leaving the noun modifier of 'mire-essence' unexposed both follow Compound concepts.
